lead.question: 早期登山者历尽艰险登上顶峰，他们真正追求的目标究竟是什么？
lead.warmup: 今天，登山者偏爱最险的路线，路线愈难愈受推崇。可在一百多年前的登山运动初期，情况恰好相反：那时的人只想找一条最省力的路登上山顶，顶峰就是他们唯一的目标。本课把我们带回阿尔卑斯山区的拓荒年代，看看早期的先锋们如何在肮脏、贫穷、与世隔绝的山村里艰难跋涉，只为把顶峰踩在脚下。
goals: 掌握 climb / summit / Alpine / settlement 等登山主题词汇
理解并运用 the more..., the more... 比较结构
辨析定语从句与分词作定语，如 settlements cut off from civilization
会用 must have been 表推测、be accustomed to 等常用短语
lead.summary: 本课对比了两代登山者。现代登山者追求运动的乐趣，路线越难越受推崇；而在拓荒时代，先驱们只求以最省力的方式登顶，顶峰便是他们唯一的目标。他们冒着极度的危险，装备简陋得令今人一想就战栗，却并非刻意寻求刺激。课文还描绘了当时阿尔卑斯山村的穷困：肮脏、跳蚤猖獗的客栈，陈年的面包与劣酒，登山者只能投宿于牧师或牧羊人处。
lead.tips: 易错提醒：go out of one's way 意为不辞辛苦、特意，而非偏离道路；must have been 表对过去的肯定推测，不要误写成 must be。

questions.q: What was the main objective of early mountain climbers?
questions.zh: 早期登山者的主要目标是什么？
questions.a: The summit — the top — was the prize they sought. The early climbers were looking for the easiest way to the top, especially a summit that had never been attained before.
questions.aZh: 顶峰——也就是山顶——才是他们寻求的目标。早期登山者寻找的是通往山顶最省力的途径，尤其是前人从未登顶过的顶峰。
questions.hint: 见课文第 3 句：the summit was the prize they sought...

questions.q: How did modern alpinists choose their routes, and how was a difficult route regarded?
questions.zh: 现代登山运动员怎样选择登山路线？艰险的路线受到怎样的对待？
questions.a: They try to climb mountains by a route which will give them good sport, and the more difficult the route is, the more highly it is regarded.
questions.aZh: 他们总想找一条能带来运动乐趣的路线登山；路线愈艰险，愈受推崇。
questions.hint: 见第 1 句 the more difficult..., the more highly it is regarded.

questions.q: What were the conditions in the Alpine villages and their inns?
questions.zh: 阿尔卑斯山区的村庄和小客栈条件如何？
questions.a: Except for places like Zermatt and Chamonix, the Alpine villages were impoverished settlements cut off from civilization; the inns were dirty and flea-ridden, and the food was local cheese with bread often twelve months old, washed down with coarse wine.
questions.aZh: 除泽曼特、夏蒙尼等少数地方外，阿尔卑斯山区的小村是与世隔绝的穷乡僻壤；客栈肮脏、跳蚤猖獗，食物是当地干酪和常放了一年之久的面包，就着劣酒咽下。
questions.hint: 见课文描写 settlements 与 Such inns as there were 的两句。

questions.q: Where did climbers find shelter when a valley had no inn?
questions.zh: 当山谷里没有客栈时，登山者在哪儿找到住处？
questions.a: They found shelter wherever they could — sometimes with the local priest, sometimes with shepherds or cheese-makers.
questions.aZh: 他们只好随遇而安——有时同当地牧师住在一起，有时同牧羊人或制乳酪的人住在一起。
questions.hint: 见第 9 句 climbers found shelter wherever they could...

questions.q: Why was the change to the Alps so hard for the early climbers?
questions.zh: 对早期的登山者来说，来到阿尔卑斯山区的生活为何如此艰难？
questions.a: Because at home they were accustomed to eating seven-course dinners and sleeping between fine linen sheets, but in the Alps they faced dirt, poverty and great discomfort.
questions.aZh: 因为他们在家里过惯了一顿饭吃七道菜、睡亚麻细布床单的生活，而在阿尔卑斯山区面对的却是肮脏、贫穷和极大的不舒适。
questions.hint: 见课文末句 For men accustomed to eating seven-course dinners... must have been very hard indeed.

exercises.q: 汉译英：路线愈艰险，愈受推崇。
exercises.a: The more difficult the route is, the more highly it is regarded.

exercises.q: 汉译英：现代登山者试图找一条能带来运动乐趣的路线登山，因为顶峰是他们寻求的目标。
exercises.a: Modern alpinists try to climb mountains by a route which will give them good sport, because the summit is the prize they seek.

exercises.q: 句型转换：将定语从句改为分词短语——Alpine villages tended to be settlements which were cut off from civilization.
exercises.a: Alpine villages tended to be settlements cut off from civilization.
exercises.note: 定语从句化简为过去分词

exercises.q: 填空：They often faced difficulties and dangers ____ the most perilous nature.
exercises.note: be of the + adj + noun 结构

exercises.q: 填空：For men accustomed to ____ (eat) seven-course dinners at home...
exercises.note: be accustomed to 接动名词

exercises.q: 改错：The change to the Alps must be very hard indeed.
exercises.a: The change to the Alps must have been very hard indeed.
exercises.note: must have been 表过去推测

exercises.q: 汉译英：山谷常常连一家客栈都没有，登山者只好找到哪里就住哪里。
exercises.a: Often a valley boasted no inn at all, and climbers found shelter wherever they could.
exercises.note: wherever 引导从句，boast 表拥有

quiz.q: 现代登山者选择登山路线时，衡量标准是什么？
options: The shortest route to the top
The easiest route to the summit
The route that gives good sport — the harder, the better
The route with the finest mountain views
quiz.note: the more difficult..., the more highly it is regarded

quiz.q: 早期登山者真正寻求的是什么？
options: The easiest way to the top
The excitement of danger
A route that offers good sport
The chance to hunt in the mountains
quiz.note: summit was the prize they sought

quiz.q: 关于拓荒时代登山者的处境，哪项符合课文？
options: They deliberately looked for exciting dangers
They faced perilous dangers though ill-equipped, but did not court excitement
They were richly equipped and feared nothing
They never met any real danger
quiz.note: they did not go out of their way to court excitement

quiz.q: 下列哪项符合课文对阿尔卑斯山村的描写？
options: Every village had a comfortable inn
They were rich and rapidly became popular
Zermatt and Chamonix stayed completely unknown
They were impoverished settlements cut off from civilization, with dirty, flea-ridden inns

quiz.q: 山谷里没有客栈时，登山者怎样解决住宿？
options: They slept in tents in the open air
They gave up and went home
They stayed with the local priest, shepherds or cheese-makers
They built new hotels for themselves

quiz.q: 对过惯舒适生活的人来说，来到阿尔卑斯山区感受如何？
options: The change must have been very hard indeed
It was a pleasant and comfortable change
It made no difference to them
It was easier than life at home
quiz.note: accustomed to seven-course dinners and fine linen sheets
